about: The decision cases for the two things in this repo that decide whether a pull request may be armed to merge by itself: scripts/should-arm-automerge.sh (the repo gate, a future merge-tail bot) and flow's arm guard (plugins/flow/scripts/land/arm-decision.ts, run by flow before it arms).

Both suites run every row: scripts/test-should-arm-automerge.sh checks `gate`, plugins/flow/engine-tests/land/arm-decision.test.ts checks `guard`. A row with only one of them fails both suites, so a change to either rule has to say what the other does with the same pull request.

Each case is the `green` payload bent by one jq `mutation`, so a failure names the field. The two answers differ on purpose where the guard is not a bot: GitHub's auto-merge waits for pending checks and for mergeability on its own, so the guard lets those through, and it refuses things the repo gate never looks at (a moved head, a fork, a base other than main, a release freeze, a security path without its label). `why` says why the row exists.

cases.name: fully green PR
cases.why: The one shape both arm. If it regresses to a refusal, nothing ever merges by itself.

cases.name: already armed
cases.why: The bot skips work already done. Flow re-arms the reviewed commit after a disarm, and arming twice changes nothing.

cases.name: already queued
cases.why: A queued PR reports autoMergeRequest:null, so the bot needs its own branch or it re-arms every queued PR on every tick.

cases.name: hold label (object)
cases.why: A hold label outranks every green signal, in both payload shapes gh produces.

cases.name: conflicting
cases.why: A conflicting PR runs no CI, so the bot cannot trust its checks. GitHub never merges a conflicting PR, so an arm on one waits.

cases.name: mergeability unknown
cases.why: GitHub works mergeability out itself before an auto-merge fires.

cases.name: unresolved threads
cases.why: The guard reads no review threads. A ruleset that requires resolved conversations still blocks the merge.

cases.name: a failing check
cases.why: Security condition 1: a red required check refuses.

cases.name: a check still running
cases.why: Security condition 1: a pending check passes the guard. GitHub's auto-merge waits for it; a check stuck pending is a watcher's job, not this guard's.

cases.name: no checks at all
cases.why: Required checks that have not reported yet are pending, and pending passes the guard.

cases.name: a red check that is not required
cases.why: The guard refuses on required checks. A red check the base does not require never blocks the merge.

cases.name: a red check when the required list is unknown
cases.why: When the forge cannot say which checks are required, every check counts as required.

cases.name: a red check, required list absent
hold outranks failure
cases.why: A held PR that is also broken reports the hold, so the person sees the human signal first.

cases.name: head moved after the review
cases.why: Security condition 2: the head at arm time must be the reviewed commit.

cases.name: reviewed commit is a short SHA
cases.why: A 7-character prefix can be matched by a different commit, so only a full SHA counts as the reviewed commit.

cases.name: base is not main
cases.why: Security condition 3.

cases.name: security path without the label
cases.why: Security condition 4, from the repo's own list (guardPolicy.securityGlobs here).

cases.name: security path, label as a string
package manifest without the label
cases.why: Package manifests and lockfiles are security paths in every repo, whatever its own list says.

cases.name: nested pnpm lockfile without the label
a manifest in another case, without the label
cases.why: Built-in security paths match in any case: on macOS's case-insensitive disk, Package.json is package.json.

cases.name: a Gradle wrapper without the label
a Maven wrapper without the label
a cargo config without the label
flow's committed config without the label
cases.why: It holds land.preArm, the commands flow runs before it arms.

cases.name: file list unreadable
cases.why: A file list the forge could not give in full is never read as touching nothing.

cases.name: release freeze on
cases.why: Security condition 5: flow freeze on, set and cleared by a release process.

cases.name: from a fork
cases.why: Security condition 6.
